items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21

ctx.x: Yeah. I said, Louie, did you get them? Yeah. I said, well you had two. I went to the toilet, I stopped the toilet. See I couldn't go. Once I go in the cavalry, I had to stay in there. Because the cops would chase me. Because I was underage, I ain't got no business down there. But my boys being a good family. You're supposed to be 21 to work there, huh? Yeah. See I could go on one side of the street, but the cops on this corner knowed me. See you had two cops here, two cops here, two cops over there, two cops over…

Oh yeah? Well let's, let's, well you know, we can all join in. Yeah. How did you first start, Rosie? Well I started on Clark Street, Chicago, just when I was a kid going to school. Are you a, are you a Chicagoan? Yes, I'm born and raised in Chicago. I didn't know the north side. Everyone thinks I was raised in the south side, but I wasn't. It'd be right up south side. I used to live on the south side and I had music, Joe Alvarez. Who were the first people you heard on the south side? Joe Alvarez. Joe Alvarez. No,…
You heard Sugar? No, no, no. Did you hear Sugar Johnny? No. Freddie Kepler. Freddie Kepler, well Freddie Kepler and Joe, yeah.

items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: And I know you all had been friends for years.

ctx.x: Mm-hmm. You're asking me to go way back now, you know, a little baby. That's kind of tough.

Another trumpet player I mentioned briefly, the last time I heard you in Chicago, Natty Dominic and I went up there at the Blue Note to hear that. Yes, I remember that. And I know you all had been friends for years. Did you hear him in the old days? Oh, yes.
Like, early, too? Mm-hmm. Dominic was good. He was all right.
